notes: In I:p5-b0 the trailing superscripts after the catalog names are reference markers, not part of the identifiers; T:p5-b0 gives them as reference 1 Brown et al. (2005), reference 2 Hirsch et al. (2005), and reference 3 Edelmann et al. (2005). HVS4 (SDSS J091301.0+305120) and HVS5 (SDSS J091759.5+672238) are the two new HVSs that T:p2-b13 explicitly calls clearly unbound, so they are candidates_found. HVS1 (SDSS J090745.0+024507), HVS2 (US 708), and HVS3 (HE 0437-5439) are prior HVS identifications relayed at T:p1-b7 and T:p1-b8, included in the paper's five-known-HVS summary at T:p3-b8; because HVSs are defined as unbound at T:p1-b9, I record these prior objects as follow_up.

HVS1: Target HVS1 = SDSS J090745.0+024507. No equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for HVS1. Reported velocities are radial-only, so v_RF = +709 km/s is explicitly a lower limit on the true space velocity (T:p5-b0). Table 1 lists v_RF without an uncertainty, while T:p1-b7 gives +709 ± 12 km s^-1 for HVS1. Galactic rest-frame velocities follow the paper's definition (heliocentric velocities corrected to the LSR with the 220 km/s solar reflex motion removed; T:p2-b7, T:p2-b9).

HVS2: The target identifiers HVS2 and US 708 both refer to the star US 708 (Hirsch et al. 2005), listed as HVS2 in Table 1 (l = 176.0 deg, b = 47.1 deg, g' = 18.8, t_GC = 32 Myr); it is distinct from the paper's newly discovered HVS5 = SDSS J091759.5+672238. Only Galactic coordinates (l, b) are given for HVS2, not equatorial RA/Dec, so no ra/dec are recorded. The paper reports only a Galactic rest-frame radial velocity ("at least +717 km/s", minimum v_RF) for HVS2, not a heliocentric radial velocity, so no radial_velocity entry is made. No galactocentric radius, proper motions, or bound/unbound probabilities are reported for this star.

HVS3: The paper reports for HVS3 (= HE 0437-5439) only Galactic coordinates (l, b) = (263.0 deg, -40.9 deg), g' = 16.2 mag, v_RF, heliocentric distance d, and travel time t_GC = 100 Myr (Table 1, T:p5-b0 / I:p5-b0); no equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motions, heliocentric radial velocity, galactocentric radius, or bound/unbound probabilities are given for this star. Table 1 gives v_RF = +548 with no error, while the text (T:p1-b8) states the velocity is at least +548 km/s, so it is recorded as a lower bound; T:p3-b8 confirms v_RF is a minimum velocity, not the full space velocity. The text attributes this star to Edelmann et al. (2005) and notes it may be a hypervelocity star ejected from the LMC rather than the Galactic Center, which is why any travel-time/Galactic-Center-origin interpretation is conditional. The ~60 kpc distance in the text and the 61 kpc value in Table 1 are both reported as distinct adopted values.

HVS5: The paper does not explicitly tabulate equatorial RA/Dec; these values are taken from the SDSS J2000 identifier SDSS J091759.5+672238 reported in the HVS5 row of T:p5-b0. The paper reports v_RF=+638±12 km/s as a minimum Galactic rest-frame velocity, not a full space velocity (T:p2-b13; also T:p3-b7), so it is treated as a lower limit on the total Galactic rest-frame speed. Two distance scales are reported: 55 kpc for the adopted B8 main-sequence interpretation (T:p3-b3, T:p5-b0) and ≃18 kpc for the alternative BHB interpretation (T:p3-b2). The Galactocentric radius ≃60 kpc corresponds to the B8 distance interpretation (T:p3-b3).

HVS4: At T:p2-b13 the paper states HVS4 and HVS5 have v_RF = +558 ± 12 and +638 ± 12 km/s (heliocentric +603 and +543 km/s); T:p3-b7 states that the radial velocities provide only a lower limit to the true space velocities. I therefore record the Galactic-rest-frame value for HVS4 as a lower limit rather than a full three-dimensional speed, and note the ±12 km/s uncertainty in its condition. Equatorial coordinates are not tabulated separately; RA/Dec are encoded in the SDSS designation in T:p5-b0. The paper gives alternative distances depending on whether HVS4 is B8 (T:p3-b3; Table 1 at T:p5-b0) or a BHB (T:p3-b2); both are retained. No numeric parallax, proper motion, bound/unbound probability, or total Galactic-rest-frame speed is reported.
